headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: shared file-based workflows plus broad egress can expose sensitive support data and API keys.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents, PDFs, HTML, MHTML, XLSX, DOC/DOCX and chat transcripts, while ms-swift reads/writes files and processes stdin/stdout in CLI/Python workflows. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content in A influence B’s parsing or prompts. No direct bridge is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or copied outputs are reused as inputs
IF B parses A-generated text as instructions or configuration
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent
Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs into B
Add a manual review step before B consumes A-produced files
Use read-only mounts for A’s export folder
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and broad document classes, and ms-swift has filesystem read/write plus allowlisted network egress. If they share a workspace, B can read A’s files and transmit sensitive content or secrets to external services. The pairwise path is plausible in default file-based workflows, so the blast radius includes exfiltration.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same filesystem path
IF A stores API keys or sensitive documents in its workspace
IF B sends read files to an external API or hub
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared directories
Use separate OS users or containers
Restrict B’s network egress to required endpoints only
Rotate any keys that may have been exposed
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift can write files, execute shell, install packages, and spawn subprocesses; kotaemon supports multiple instances and uses a local data directory. Even without modify_git_state, overlapping writes to shared files or configs can race and corrupt outputs. The profiles do not state locking or isolation, so conflict is plausible and not blocked.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or config file
IF multiple instances of kotaemon run alongside one ms-swift session
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Run only one writer per workspace
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Snapshot outputs before handoff
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon is a RAG/chat system that can generate citations and answers, and ms-swift can consume files and run CLI/Python workflows. If B treats A’s generated text as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream training, evaluation, or support artifacts. No verification mechanism is documented between them, so the pathway exists.
conditions: IF B ingests A-generated summaries, citations, or transcripts without verification
IF A’s outputs are used as training or evaluation inputs
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them
Compare A outputs against source documents
Keep A outputs labeled as untrusted
Use checksum-based handoff files
requires-engineering: add validation gates before B actions

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon handles API keys and customer-support documents, while ms-swift touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration data. Their documented data classes and retention surfaces differ, so the same support content could be retained or logged differently across the pair. No residency or certification mismatch is stated, so this is a policy-gap risk rather than a breach claim.
conditions: IF the same customer-support data is processed by both agents
IF B logs or checkpoints contain data that A would otherwise keep transient
mitigations: Classify data before handing it to either agent
Disable or minimize logging for sensitive runs
Set explicit retention limits for outputs
Keep regulated data out of training/checkpoint paths
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
